title: Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle
alloyReason: Ti-6Al-4V ELI (Grade 23, UNS R56401) is mandated for this oil & gas application where ELI elements (O <=0.13%, Fe <=0.25%) provide superior fracture toughness (KIC >100 MPa-m0.5) and fatigue resistance vs standard Grade 5. This rationale is driven by offshore platform firewater deluge nozzle and specific design requirements.
process: Ring forging radial-axial for oil & gas geometry
CNC turn-bore operation for net-shape tolerance
TIG welding autogenous for net-shape tolerance
Hydrostatic pressure test for net-shape tolerance
surfaceTreatment: Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for offshore platform firewater application
inspection: UT wall thickness scan (offshore platform verified)
commonFailures: Crevice corrosion under biofouling in stagnant seawater - mitigated by CP-Ti Grade 2 + ICCP system — critical for offshore platform firewater performance

faq.q: What specific material properties make Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle suitable for Offshore platform firewater deluge nozzle?
faq.a: Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle uses Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V because its yield strength, fatigue endurance, and corrosion resistance directly address oil & gas operational demands. The alloy's specific strength enables mass reduction without section compromise, while the TiO2 passivation ensures long-term environmental resistance.

faq.q: What are the critical dimensional tolerances for Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle?
faq.a: Standard machining tolerance for Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle is +/-0.05mm (ISO 2768-m). Functional mating surfaces are held to +/-0.025mm with Ra 0.8um finish, verified specifically for offshore platform firewater requirements. Threaded features conform to ISO 965-2 Class 6g, verified with calibrated Go/No-Go ring gauges on 100% of production.

faq.q: Does Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle require any post-machining surface treatment?
faq.a: Yes. offshore platform firewater components require Heavy-duty passivation 25% HNO3 45min per ASTM B600 for maximum chloride pitting resistance in seawater — tailored for offshore platform firewater application. This restores the natural TiO2 passive layer removed during machining and provides the required surface properties for the specific service environment. Key parameters include surface finish Ra 0.8um and passive layer thickness verification per applicable standards.

faq.q: What quality documentation is included with Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle shipments?
faq.a: Each shipment of Titanium Offshore Firewater Nozzle includes: (1) EN 10204 Type 3.1 MTR with full chemical analysis and mechanical properties; (2) Certificate of Conformance confirming all processes meet offshore platform firewater specifications; (3) Dimensional inspection report with actual vs nominal measurements on critical features; (4) Surface roughness certification per applicable standards. FAIR available on request.

faq.q: What is the MOQ and typical lead time for Firewater nozzle / Deluge head oil & gas components?
faq.a: Standard MOQ: 1 unit for prototype evaluation. Production lead time: 15-25 business days depending on quantity. Rush orders (3-5 days) available. Contact our supply chain team for volume-based tiered pricing.
